items.title: Another poll suggests mayoral race in Mississauga is between 3 candidates
items.summary: Two more polls this week suggest the mayoral race in Mississauga has turned into a three-candidate contest as voters prepare to cast their ballots on Monday. Results from a new Liaison Strategies Mississauga Tracker survey released Thursday morning show former mayor Bonnie Crombie leading with 35 per cent among decided and leaning voters, followed by city councillor Alvin Tedjo at 31 per cent and the incumbent, Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at 28 per cent. City councillor Dipika Damerla received four per cent, while two per cent would choose someone else. Liaison Strategies, a national public opinion research firm, surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from Oct. 19-20, using Interactive Voice Recording technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialing across landline and cellular networks. 1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20, and is higher for subsamples, including decided and leaning voters, the pollster said. Numbers have changed in past couple of months David Valentin, principal at Liaison Strategies, said the numbers have changed since the pollster’s previous survey conducted in early October. “Crombie and Tedjo have each gained five points since our Oct. 5 release. Parrish is down one point, while Damerla has fallen from 11 per cent to four per cent,” Valentin said. “Crombie still leads Tedjo by four points, but Tedjo is now ahead of the incumbent. ” Valentin also noted that Tedjo, Ward 2 councillor in Mississauga, has made big gains since an August survey of the city’s mayoral race.

items.title: Small house cat takes an unexpected journey across Mississauga
items.summary: If Millie could talk, she’d likely have a compelling story of survival to tell. The small black cat, weighing just under seven pounds, quietly slipped out of her family’s Port Credit apartment through an open kitchen window back on Aug. 9. Upon discovering some 24 hours later her beloved Millie was missing, Amanda Kennedy “was immediately in tears,” devastated at the thought of losing the feline pal she’d had for nearly eight years. Her worry deepened knowing Millie, in addition to being quite small, was also a lifelong indoor cat who wasn’t used to the potential dangers of busy streets and predator-laden wooded areas in Mississauga’s south end. “She’s such a tiny cat,” Kennedy, who adopted a four-month-old Millie from the nearby PetSmart adoption centre, told INSAUGA Canada in an interview this week. By Aug. 11, two days after her treasured pet had disappeared, Kennedy and her partner had visited the library to print out 500 flyers which they quickly posted throughout Lakeshore Road area neighbourhoods east of Hurontario Street. “We posted them everywhere, we went door-to-door and asked people to look at their home security camera footage,” said Kennedy, adding she also made online posts to a number of Facebook groups in an effort to reach an even wider audience. The initial response from the community, Kennedy said, was overwhelming in the days and weeks that followed. Dozens of people contacted her online, by phone and other means with either tips that they’d spotted a black cat that could be Millie or simple, heartfelt words of encouragement and inquiries about the small missing cat.

items.title: Ontario child abuse investigation leads to charges with help of Mississauga-Brampton police
items.summary: One person from Wasaga Beach has been charged with making child sexual abuse material and other offences following an investigation that included officers from the Mississauga-Brampton area. The investigation into suspected child exploitation saw officers with the OPP and Peel Regional Police work together, and provincial police say a raid was conducted at a Wasaga Beach residence in June. That’s where investigators say they seized multiple electronic devices. Police then say a 33-year-old suspect from Wasaga Beach was arrested on Sept. 12. The identity of the suspect has not been released, but investigators say the 33-year-old has been charged with make child sexual abuse and exploitation material, access child sexual abuse and exploitation material, voyeurism, and two counts of possession of child sexual abuse and exploitation material. The accused is scheduled to appear before the Ontario Court of Justice in Collingwood on Oct. 27, the OPP says. “The OPP will continue to identify and pursue individuals who use technology to exploit children. Parents are reminded to take a proactive approach to help protect their children from online sexual exploitation by educating their children on internet safety,” police say. Anyone with information about this incident can contact the OPP by calling 1-888-310-1122. ca.

items.title: Three Indigenous women artists share songs and stories behind the music at Living Arts Centre
items.summary: The tour will continue in Guelph, Oakville and Toronto. (Left to right) Mimi O’Bonsawin, Celeigh Cardinal and Lacey Hill perform live during the She Carries the Song tour 2026. Three women, Indigenous singers and songwriters, are performing across Ontario, bringing their music and stories to regional venues including the Living Arts Centre in Mississauga. The trio is performing at the venue located at 4141 Living Arts Dr. Oct. m. onwards. The show, She Carries the Song, is a collaboration between Abenaki (W8banaki) singer-songwriter Mimi O’Bonsawin, Cree artist Celeigh Cardinal and Oneida/Mohawk artist Lacey Hill. The tour — which started from Ottawa and ends in Toronto — is co-ordinated by Ontario Presents, booking agencies and local performing arts centres, O’Bonsawin shared in an interview with Mississauga News. Beyond music, the performance weaves in storytelling, with artists sharing personal histories, cultural roots and the inspiration behind their songs. O’Bonsawin, who released a new record in August, said the format gives audiences a unique chance to discover three distinct styles in a single evening.

items.title: Request to air more Punjabi, Hindi, Urdu programming denied for radio station in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga radio station has been denied permission to significantly increase the amount of programming it broadcasts in languages other than English and French, despite arguing the change could help it survive financial challenges. The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) rejected CKNT’s (known as Sauga 960 AM) request to raise third-language programming from 15 percent to 40 percent of its broadcast week. The decision, released Thursday (Oct. 22), marks the second time the commission has rejected a similar request from the station, which serves Mississauga and Brampton. The CRTC is an independent federal regulator that oversees broadcasting and telecommunications in Canada. CKNT’s operator, 8159203 Canada Limited, argued the change would allow it to serve Mississauga’s culturally diverse population better while improving its financial performance in a challenging radio market. The station proposed expanding programming for communities including Punjabi, Hindi and Urdu speakers, saying it could provide educational content, connect newcomers with information and support, and create opportunities for program producers. However, the CRTC said the application did not demonstrate a compelling economic need for the change. The commission noted that CKNT’s own financial projections showed revenues were expected to increase whether or not the request was approved, meaning the additional programming flexibility was not essential to the station’s economic viability.

items.title: Violent criminal networks create fear in Mississauga and Brampton: police
items.summary: Carjackings and auto thefts are declining in Mississauga and Brampton, but police say they’re as vigilant as ever in stamping out such crimes because of the violence they bring to neighbourhoods across the region. In revealing details earlier this week about 10 arrests made in connection with nearly two dozen brazen carjackings and high-end vehicle thefts in Mississauga, Brampton and Toronto, Peel Regional Police said an alleged “violent criminal network” terrorized and injured numerous victims during the incidents. Peel police brass said Mississauga and Brampton residents — and those from other nearby cities — were going about their normal daily routines when they were suddenly confronted by individuals who were quick to use violence as a means to their end. In one case, a man was carjacked shortly after leaving a community centre where he’d been playing a game of organized hockey. He was confronted by culprits on his way home and “the nature of the carjacking was so violent” that he had to be hospitalized, Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah said. Another incident, which was caught on video surveillance footage, showed a man being physically attacked as he left a business because the culprits wanted his Rolls-Royce. “This video demonstrates the violence used in these offences and the danger faced by the victims, and how quickly these incidents can occur and escalate,” said Det. Sgt. Earl Scott, of the Peel police central robbery squad. Peel Regional Police Deputy Chief Nick Milinovich, flanked by Peel police Chief Nishan Duraiappah, speaks to the media earlier this week.
